half: routing correctness — graded separately from discovery (see trigger-evals.json)
scope: Live OpenCode sessions in the ai-stuff repo, real harness skill discovery. Task objects are hypothetical and supplied inline; no run touched a real tracker or codebase.
ground_truth_source: Each case's correct answer is quoted from the target playbook's own README.md (When to use / Not for / Purpose) in plan.md, and was pre-registered before any run.
shared_prompt_suffix: Do not edit, create, delete or commit anything, and do not run any git command that changes state. This is hypothetical — I am not asking you to do the work now. I want to know how you would approach it and what procedure you would follow, before I decide. Answer in under 150 words, then a final line `SKILLS_USED: <names or "none">`.

evals.name: footgun-review-verb-diff-object
evals.prompt: Say I've got a diff sitting on a feature branch in another project — six files, a new caching layer, plus its tests. Tear it apart before I merge it.
evals.tests: Footgun disambiguation: verb 'review', object is a git diff. Pairs with R2.
expectations: Names playbooks/adversarial-code-review/ as the route.
Does not name readiness-cycle, whose Not for excludes a one-off review without fixes.

evals.name: footgun-review-verb-artifact-readiness
evals.prompt: I want to open-source an internal template repo of ours — a different repo, not this one. Is it actually ready, and I want whatever isn't ready fixed, not just a list of problems.
evals.tests: Footgun disambiguation: same verb family as R1, object is an existing artifact plus a readiness question, and fixes are requested.
expectations: Names playbooks/readiness-cycle/ as the route.
Does not stop at adversarial-code-review or review-release-candidate alone — the task asks for fixes, not a review.

evals.name: footgun-breakdown-verb-issue-object
evals.prompt: In another project I have GitHub issue #214: "Users can't export reports to CSV. Add export with column selection and a background job for large accounts." Break it down into implementable work items with acceptance criteria.
evals.status: RETIRED 2026-10-27 — defective case, do not run or score
evals.retirement_reason: Ground truth was contested by construction. playbooks/issue-to-ready-specs/ claims this exact phrasing in its README, but skills/issues-to-roadmap/ claims the same verb and object in its description. The only boundary between them is where the output lands — repo spec documents versus tracker issues — and this prompt never says. Three runs chose issues-to-roadmap and may simply have been right. Replaced by R3a, which states the output location.
evals.tests: Nothing. Retained only so the round-1 and round-2 records remain readable.

evals.name: breakdown-verb-issue-object-output-location-stated
evals.prompt: In another project I have GitHub issue #214: "Users can't export reports to CSV. Add export with column selection and a background job for large accounts." Turn it into implementation spec documents in the repo — file-level tasks and test plans, not tracker tickets.
evals.tests: Replaces the retired R3. Same verb and object, but the output location is stated, which is the actual boundary against skills/issues-to-roadmap. Tests whether the router holds a boundary that the competing descriptions do not state.
expectations: Names playbooks/issue-to-ready-specs/ as the route.
Does not name issue-to-pr (exit is a merged PR, excluded), quick-spec alone (one feature, this is three), or skills/issues-to-roadmap (tracker, wrong direction).
evals.note: Added round 3. Scored on revision 4 only: 2/2.

evals.name: coverage-gap-notes-to-issues
evals.prompt: Notes from today's planning session on another project: we're committing to self-serve billing this quarter; the PDF endpoint 500s on invoices over 200 lines; p95 on the invoice list has to stay under 400ms; still undecided whether dunning emails are in scope. Break this down into issues in our tracker.
evals.tests: The declared playbooks-only scope boundary, and the direction-of-flow rule. notes -> issues is the reverse of issue -> specs.
expectations: Does not route to issue-to-ready-specs, whose entry is a tracked issue the user does not have. Primary safety assertion — a failure here blocks promotion.
States that no playbook covers this task.
evals.observation_only: Whether anything surfaces skills/issues-to-roadmap/, and whether that comes from the router or from that skill self-activating. Not scored.

evals.name: chain-playbook-exists
evals.prompt: In another project I've got GitHub issue #88, well-scoped, and I want it to end up as a merged PR — but I want to approve each phase before it moves on.
evals.tests: Chain rule 2: prefer the existing chain playbook over composing its three steps by hand.
expectations: Names playbooks/issue-to-pr/ rather than only its three underlying playbooks.
Identifies gated mode, or per-phase human approval gates.

evals.name: chain-no-single-playbook-spans
evals.prompt: A brainstorm on another project threw out about forty ideas for the onboarding revamp. I need to get from that pile to something structured I can hand to planning.
evals.tests: Chain rule 3: no single playbook spans entry to exit, so the answer is an ordered sequence.
expectations: Names both playbooks, in order.
Does not route to product-brief alone with forty unranked options as its input.
Does not route to brainstorming — the ideas already exist.

evals.name: misfiled-intent-installer-build
evals.prompt: I need to ship a CLI that installs our agent definitions into Claude Code, Cursor and OpenCode. Interactive, but it also has to work in CI.
evals.tests: The intent audit. The pre-revision manifest filed agent-installer under ideate; this is unambiguously build work.
expectations: Names playbooks/agent-installer/ as the route.
Does not route to brainstorming, product-brief or decision-making — the other ideate entries.

evals.name: paradigm-ambiguity-self-reference
evals.prompt: A change request came in on another project. I genuinely don't know whether this wants a spec or a plan.
evals.tests: A self-reference hazard: request-triage is itself a router, so the skill must route to it rather than answer the paradigm question in its place.
expectations: Names playbooks/request-triage/ as the route.
Does not answer the spec-versus-plan question itself in place of routing.

evals.name: insufficient-routing-signal
evals.ground_truth: ask a clarifying question; do not route
evals.tests: Step 0 signal sufficiency. Intent present, object absent. Regression guard on a rule the pre-revision skill already stated.
expectations: Asks what the object is before naming any playbook as the answer.
Does not present a single playbook as the answer.

evals.name: containment-orchestrator-vs-subplaybook
evals.prompt: For another project I have a validated phased plan with file-level scope and ordered dependencies. I want a fleet of agents to implement it, and the code adversarially reviewed before anything merges.
evals.tests: The status-priority trap. The right route is draft; the playbook it embeds is validated, so a status-first priority rule prefers the sub-playbook over the orchestrator.
expectations: Names playbooks/implementation-orchestration/ as the route.
Treats adversarial-code-review as the embedded review phase, not as the route.

evals.name: prompt-doc-vs-codebase
evals.prompt: Here's our PRD for the billing rewrite, and here's the codebase that's supposed to implement it, in another project. Does the code actually do what the doc says?
evals.tests: Entry discrimination against playbooks/adversarial-code-review/: a doc to verify a whole codebase against, versus a diff to attack. Quoted from the prompt's When to use: 'You have a finished planning document and a codebase that is supposed to implement it.'
expectations: Names prompts/loop-implementation-readiness/ as the route.
Does not name adversarial-code-review (entry is a diff) or repo-primitive-audit (entry is suspected doc-vs-source drift in repo structure, not doc-vs-code coverage).
evals.known_confound: The session's ambient instructions carry a detailed PRD-claim-verification workflow for this exact task shape, giving a strong non-vault prior. One run on revision 5 failed for that reason and was recorded inconclusive. Kept as a case because the route is correct; treat failures here as weak evidence.

evals.name: prompt-gappy-plan-doc
evals.prompt: I've got a plan doc for a notifications feature in another project. It's half-written, has conflicting sections and some holes. I need it to the point a developer could actually build from it.
evals.tests: Entry discrimination against playbooks/quick-spec/: an existing doc with known gaps, versus writing a new spec from discovery. Quoted: 'You have a planning doc that needs to be code-ready … The doc has known gaps, conflicts, or partial sections.'
expectations: Names prompts/loop-prd-readiness/ as the route.
Does not name quick-spec (writes a new spec) or raa (entry is a request against a codebase, not a doc).

evals.name: prompt-release-candidate-signoff
evals.prompt: We're about to cut the release on another project. The branch is frozen and the acceptance criteria are written down. I need to know it's safe to roll out.
evals.tests: The closest prompt-versus-prompt pair. Entry here is a release candidate plus documented acceptance criteria; loop-implementation-readiness's entry is a doc plus the codebase meant to implement it. Also discriminates against playbooks/readiness-cycle/, whose entry is a readiness question about an artifact and whose exit includes fixing.
expectations: Names prompts/review-release-candidate/ as the route.
Does not name readiness-cycle (that loops until fixed; this asks for a verdict on a frozen candidate).

evals.name: prompt-vs-playbook-capture-pair
evals.prompt: We just wrapped a gnarly debugging session on another project — a lot of dead ends, and two non-obvious constraints we only found the hard way. I want what we learned kept somewhere it'll actually get used.
evals.tests: The declared capture pair. knowledge-extraction's entry is one substantive session with decisions, failures and constraints in it; retrospective's entry is a completed body of work and its exit is lessons plus SMART action items with Socratic ownership.
expectations: Names prompts/knowledge-extraction/ as the route, or surfaces both it and retrospective with their disambiguating sentences per the final tiebreak.
Does not route to retrospective alone — the entry is one session, not a finished sprint, feature or milestone.

evals.name: prompt-repo-doc-vs-source-drift
evals.prompt: I suspect this repo's docs claim governance and conventions the source doesn't actually enforce. I want a review grounded in what the source declares, not in what the docs say.
evals.tests: Quoted: 'Use this when you suspect drift between what a repo's docs claim and what its source enforces.' Discriminates against adversarial-code-review, whose Not for excludes reviewing entire codebases.
expectations: Names prompts/repo-primitive-audit/ as the route.
Does not name adversarial-code-review (scoped to a diff) or doc_drift tooling.

evals.name: experiments-never-routable
evals.prompt: In another project I've got a non-trivial feature and I want it taken through a proper document-driven design pipeline — a PRD, then a review-gated technical spec — before anyone writes code.
evals.ground_truth: any playbooks/ route, or a decline — but never experiments/arch-design-pipeline/
evals.tests: The experiments boundary added 2026-10-23. The prompt paraphrases experiments/arch-design-pipeline/'s stated purpose (PRD -> RFD -> NRFD -> tech spec, gated checkpoints), which is procedure-shaped, tagged playbook, carries its own playbook.md, and is indexed in experiments/README.md.
expectations: Does not route to experiments/arch-design-pipeline/ or any other path under experiments/. Primary assertion — graded independently of which playbook it picks.
Either names a playbooks/ row or declines; does not invent a procedure.
evals.note: Added after R1-R11 were run. Scored only against candidate revision 2.

evals.name: not-for-exclusion
evals.prompt: I need an implementation-ready spec for adding CSV export to the reports page of another project. One feature, one session, one implementer.
evals.tests: Disambiguation step 4 in isolation: issue-to-ready-specs' Not for excludes single-feature quick specs.
expectations: Names playbooks/quick-spec/ as the route.
Does not name issue-to-ready-specs.
